Gluconeogenesis defect with lactic acidosis and defining neurodevelopmental impairment; developmental delay in 17/17. Hepatomegaly is occasional.
Pure anxiety disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
APC-associated attenuated polyposis directly produces colorectal adenomas; extracolonic organ damage is not consistently common.
Fucosylation defect with severe developmental impairment; limb undergrowth 3/3 and skeletal abnormalities; glaucoma 1/3. Cardiac and renal findings (1/3 each) omitted at cap; small cohort.
Congenital absence of central incisor teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Meningeal tumour; radiation identifies its cause without changing its organ of origin.
Accessory cardiac conduction pathway causing ventricular pre-excitation and arrhythmias.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and progressive visual loss affect most late-infantile cases.
Hereditary nephropathy with renal insufficiency in 6/6. Hearing impairment reported in only 1/6; no qualifying ocular evidence.
Inherited epidermal disorder with seborrhea-like dermatitis, hyperkeratosis and acanthosis; autoimmune disease is not established.
Inherited myocardial disease encompassing hypertrophic, dilated, restrictive and noncompaction cardiomyopathy.
Stenosis directly affects the carotid artery. Stroke is a separately diagnosed complication, not universal neurologic involvement.
Definition places this mixed sarcomatous tumour in soft tissues or the nervous system; both origins are represented.
Reactive cytokine-driven eosinophilia with tissue injury; persistent cutaneous involvement occurs in roughly half. Cardiac and pulmonary damage vary across reactive causes.
Mediastinum is outside the explicitly listed organ territories; this site-only concept specifies no pulmonary, cardiac, neural or other covered organ of origin.
Nonsyndromic CRYGS-associated lens cataract.
Defined as focal dystonia of pelvic floor skeletal muscles, causing impaired relaxation during defecation.
Major congenital cardiac malformations dominate. Situs changes alone do not establish organ damage; asplenia in 4/14 (~29%) is borderline and omitted.
Hypogonadism and intellectual disability with microcephaly define the syndrome; syndactyly frequency is unspecified.
Fibrosis and regenerative nodules replace liver parenchyma. Varices and hepatic encephalopathy are separately diagnosed complications.
Isolated inherited platelet disorder with thrombocytopenia and enlarged platelets.
The syndrome is defined by muscular dystrophy and spongiform degeneration of cerebral white matter.
Mast-cell-mediated cutaneous disease producing urticarial wheals; skin lesions define the disease even when individual lesions are transient.
Congenital contractures, neck pterygia and scoliosis accompany defining congenital heart defects or cardiomyopathy.
